context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a public and academic platform for cataloguing physical and digital items, managing circulation, and providing self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search requirements.

## Key Elements
* `Library Patron`: External actor accessing self-service portals
* `Librarian`: External actor managing cataloguing and circulation
* `Library Management System`: Core software system boundary
* `Identity Provider (IdP)`: External system for SSO authentication
* `Payment Gateway`: External system for processing fines and fees
* `Notification Provider`: External system for sending circulation alerts

## Relationships
* `Library Patron` & `Librarian` -> `Library Management System` (HTTPS, TLS 1.3)
* `Library Management System` -> `Identity Provider` (OAuth2/OIDC, HTTPS)
* `Library Management System` -> `Payment Gateway` (REST/HTTPS)
* `Library Management System` -> `Notification Provider` (SMTPS/HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
* `OAuth2/OIDC`: Delegated authentication protocol
* `TLS 1.3`: Transport security for all inbound and outbound traffic
* `EU Data Centers`: Frankfurt/Dublin regions for data residency compliance
* `Encrypted Secrets Manager`: Secure credential management isolated from source code

## Rationale
The architecture strictly delegates credential handling to an external IdP and enforces mTLS/TLS 1.3 to secure boundaries. Confining deployments to EU data centers satisfies regulatory compliance and search performance constraints.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It is engineered to satisfy EU-only data residency and sub-800ms search performance requirements.

## Key Elements
- Library Patron and Librarian (Users)
- Identity Provider (IdP), Payment Gateway, and Notification Provider (External Systems)
- Web Frontend: React SPA served via Nginx
- API Gateway: Spring Cloud Gateway
- Microservices: Catalogue Service, Circulation Service, and Notification Service (Spring Boot / Java 21)
- Data & Messaging: PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, and RabbitMQ
- Infrastructure: Istio service mesh and HashiCorp Vault

## Relationships
- Library Patron/Librarian to Web Frontend via HTTPS/REST and WebSockets
- Web Frontend to API Gateway via HTTPS/REST
- API Gateway to Microservices via internal gRPC with mTLS and propagated JWTs
- Microservices to PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch via encrypted database protocols (AES-256)
- Microservices to RabbitMQ via AMQP over TLS
- External integrations (IdP, Payment Gateway, Notification Provider) via TLS 1.3

## Technology Stack
- Java 21 / Spring Boot: Standardized backend runtime to reduce operational and polyglot complexity
- Spring Cloud Gateway: Handles ingress routing, rate limiting, and OAuth2/OIDC validation
- PostgreSQL: Relational data store for structured catalogue and circulation data
- Elasticsearch: Dedicated search engine ensuring 99th-percentile search responses under 800ms
- RabbitMQ: Asynchronous message broker with dead-letter exchanges
- Istio / Envoy: Service mesh enforcing automated mTLS and distributed trace propagation via OpenTelemetry

## Rationale
Standardizing on a unified Java 21 Spring Boot stack simplifies operational pipelines while satisfying the strict EU data residency constraint. Furthermore, the combination of Elasticsearch, gRPC, and an Istio service mesh directly addresses high-performance search SLAs and zero-trust security mandates.

Web Frontend.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries within the EU. The architecture utilizes a React SPA frontend hosted on Nginx communicating with Spring Boot microservices via an API Gateway.

## Key Elements
- Library Patron, Librarian (Users)
- Web Frontend (React SPA, Nginx Container)
- Routing & Shell Component, Catalog Component, Circulation Component, API Client Component, Auth & Session Component (Frontend Components)
- API Gateway (Spring Cloud Gateway)
- Catalogue Service, Circulation Service, Notification Service (Spring Boot, Java 21)
- PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch (Databases), RabbitMQ (Message Broker)

## Relationships
- Library Patron / Librarian -> Web Frontend: Accesses portals via `HTTPS/REST` and `WSS://` (WebSockets)
- Web Frontend -> API Gateway: Sends API requests via `HTTPS/REST` with W3C Trace Context headers (`traceparent`) and HttpOnly cookies
- API Gateway -> Catalogue Service / Circulation Service: Routes internal requests

## Technology Stack
- React / React Router: UI framework and routing for client-side rendering
- Nginx: Web server configured with strict CSP headers, TLS 1.3, and EU-only data residency hosting
- TanStack Query: Client-side state management and pagination to meet <800ms search latency
- Axios: HTTP and WebSocket transport client

## Rationale
Client-side caching and pagination ensure 99th-percentile search responses remain under 800 ms. Strict Nginx security headers and secure cookie management protect patron data while complying with EU data residency constraints.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
- The system is an API Gateway container for the Library Management System, providing secure ingress routing, traffic throttling, and protocol translation.
- Its core purpose is to enforce security policies and high-performance request dispatching to satisfy strict EU data residency and sub-800ms search latency requirements.

## Key Elements
- API Gateway (Spring Cloud Gateway, Java 21)
- Routing & Dispatcher Component (Spring Cloud Gateway Core)
- Authentication & Authorization Filter (Spring Security OAuth2 Resource Server)
- Rate Limiting & Throttling Filter (Redis-backed Token Bucket)
- Resilience & Circuit Breaker Filter (Resilience4j)
- Web Frontend, Catalogue Service, Circulation Service, Notification Service, IdP

## Relationships
- Web Frontend -> API Gateway: Sends API requests via [HTTPS/REST] with TLS 1.3
- Web Frontend -> Authentication & Authorization Filter: Validates user sessions via [HTTPS/REST]
- Authentication & Authorization Filter -> Routing & Dispatcher Component: Forwards validated requests via [Internal Java Method Call]
- Routing & Dispatcher Component -> Resilience & Circuit Breaker Filter: Passes requests for fault-tolerance checks via [Internal Java Method Call]
- Resilience & Circuit Breaker Filter -> Catalogue Service / Circulation Service / Notification Service: Routes protected calls via [gRPC with mTLS, propagated JWTs, OpenTelemetry headers]

## Technology Stack
- Spring Cloud Gateway (Java 21): Reactive model selected for non-blocking I/O and performance
- Spring Security OAuth2: Handles OIDC token validation and audience checks
- Redis: Localized cluster instance used for token-bucket rate limiting within EU nodes
- Resilience4j: Implements circuit breakers and bulkheading for downstream fault tolerance
- OpenTelemetry: Injects distributed trace contexts at the edge for latency tracking
- Kubernetes Secrets: Secures ingestion of IdP client secrets and mTLS certificates

## Rationale
- The reactive Spring Cloud Gateway architecture and non-blocking components minimize overhead to meet the <800ms search SLA.
- Localized Redis clustering, TLS 1.3 hardening, and strict PII masking in logs and rate limit keys ensure total EU data residency and privacy compliance.

Catalogue Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The architecture enforces strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Library Patron, Librarian
- **External Systems**: Identity Provider (IdP), Payment Gateway, Notification Provider
- **Containers**: Web Frontend (React SPA, Nginx), API Gateway (Spring Cloud Gateway), Catalogue Service (Spring Boot, Java 21), Circulation Service, Notification Service, PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, RabbitMQ
- **Catalogue Service Components**: Catalogue Controller, Catalogue Manager, Search Component, Repository Component, Outbox Publisher Component

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Catalogue Controller: gRPC with mTLS and propagated JWTs
- Catalogue Manager -> Search Component: In-memory Java method calls
- Catalogue Manager -> Outbox Publisher Component: In-memory domain event dispatch
- Outbox Publisher Component -> RabbitMQ: AMQP over TLS 1.3
- RabbitMQ -> Search Component: Event consumer listener over TLS 1.3
- Search Component -> Elasticsearch: Bolt/REST over TLS 1.3
- Repository Component -> PostgreSQL: Encrypted database protocols (AES-256)
- Catalogue Service -> Identity Provider (IdP): TLS 1.3

## Technology Stack
- **Spring Boot / Java 21**: Core application framework for the Catalogue Service.
- **PostgreSQL**: Relational persistence managed via Spring Data JPA with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE).
- **Elasticsearch**: Indexing and search engine for high-performance catalog queries.
- **RabbitMQ**: Asynchronous messaging broker utilizing the outbox pattern.
- **Resilience4j**: Circuit breaking and fallback handling.
- **HashiCorp Vault**: Secret management for dynamic runtime credential injection.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples the write and read paths using an asynchronous outbox pattern over RabbitMQ, ensuring 99th-percentile search response times remain under the 800 ms SLA. Strict encryption, mTLS, and localized EU persistent volume claims satisfy compliance and data residency constraints.

Circulation Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Circulation Service is a core container of the Library Management System responsible for managing borrowing, returns, and fine workflows. It ensures high performance, strict EU data residency, and reliable transaction processing for academic and public libraries.

## Key Elements
- **Circulation Controller / GrpcHandler**: Exposes gRPC endpoints [Java/gRPC].
- **Borrowing Engine**: Manages loan logic including the **Loan Rule Engine (Specification Pattern)** [Spring Service / Java 21].
- **Fine Management Component**: Handles fee calculations with **Resilience4j** circuit breaking.
- **Circulation Data Access Object (DAO)**: Manages persistence via **Spring Data JPA / Hibernate**.
- **Outbox Pattern Component**: Guarantees reliable messaging via local transactions.
- **Event Publisher**: Publishes domain events [Spring AMQP].

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Circulation Controller: Routes requests [gRPC with mTLS, JWT]
- Circulation DAO -> PostgreSQL: Persists data [Encrypted database protocols, AES-256]
- Event Publisher -> RabbitMQ: Publishes messages [AMQP over TLS]
- Fine Management Component -> Payment Gateway: Processes fees [TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- **Spring Boot / Java 21**: Core application framework for modular architecture and robust concurrency.
- **PostgreSQL**: Primary transactional data store ensuring EU-only data residency compliance.
- **RabbitMQ**: Message broker for asynchronous, decoupled event distribution.
- **gRPC with mTLS**: High-performance internal service-to-service communication protocol.
- **Resilience4j**: Fault tolerance library preventing downstream cascading failures.
- **OpenTelemetry**: Distributed tracing standard for system observability.

## Rationale
This architecture uses modular Spring Boot services with gRPC communication to meet strict performance requirements like sub-800ms searches. The Outbox pattern and robust security controls ensure data integrity, transactional reliability, and EU data residency compliance.

Notification Service.analysis:
## Overview
[Library Management System] is a comprehensive solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals.

## Key Elements
* Notification Controller (Spring Web/gRPC)
* Event Consumer / Listener (Spring AMQP)
* Template Engine (Thymeleaf)
* Dispatch Engine (Java 21 Service Layer)
* Provider Integration Client (Spring WebClient with Resilience4j)
* Outbox Table (PostgreSQL with JPA/Hibernate)
* RabbitMQ (Message Broker)
* Notification Provider (External API)
* HashiCorp Vault (Secret Management)

## Relationships
* API Gateway -> Notification Controller: gRPC with mTLS and propagated JWTs
* Event Consumer -> RabbitMQ: AMQP over TLS
* Notification Controller / Event Consumer -> Outbox Table: JDBC over TLS
* Dispatch Engine -> Provider Integration Client: In-process Java method calls
* Provider Integration Client -> Notification Provider: Outbound REST over TLS 1.3
* Provider Integration Client -> HashiCorp Vault: Secure secret retrieval

## Technology Stack
* Java 21 & Spring Boot: Core runtime and framework for robust service implementation
* PostgreSQL: Relational database utilizing the Outbox Pattern for reliable transactional messaging
* RabbitMQ: Asynchronous message broker for handling event-driven alerts
* Resilience4j: Circuit breaker implementation to protect external provider calls and fail fast
* Thymeleaf: Secure template engine enforcing strict escaping to prevent SSTI
* OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing across gRPC boundaries, RabbitMQ headers, and TLS requests

## Rationale
This component architecture implements strict EU-only data residency constraints through regional provider mandates, PII redaction, and encrypted outbox storage. It guarantees high performance, transactional reliability, and security using resilience patterns and token-bucket rate limiting.

## Overview
The PostgreSQL component provides a secure, highly available relational data store for the Library Management System. It manages structured catalogue and circulation data while enforcing strict EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
- Relational Engine (PostgreSQL 16)
- Storage Subspace
- Connection Pooler (PgBouncer)
- Schema Partitioning Component
- Audit Logging Component (pgaudit)

## Relationships
- Catalogue Service -> Connection Pooler: SQL/TCP [TLS 1.3, mTLS, SCRAM-SHA-256]
- Circulation Service -> Connection Pooler: SQL/TCP [TLS 1.3, mTLS, SCRAM-SHA-256]
- Connection Pooler -> Relational Engine: Inter-process socket [TLS 1.3]
- Relational Engine -> Storage Subspace: File I/O [AES-256, TDE]
- Relational Engine -> Schema Partitioning: Logical isolation [Internal]

## Technology Stack
- PostgreSQL 16: Core relational engine for ACID transactions and data storage
- PgBouncer: Connection pooling to prevent thread exhaustion from microservices
- Kubernetes StatefulSets & CloudNativePG: High availability and automated failover
- pgaudit & pgcrypto: Compliance auditing and column-level encryption for GDPR

## Rationale
This architecture uses connection pooling and schema isolation to maintain microservice boundaries and meet performance goals. Kubernetes operators, encryption, and automated backups ensure high availability and strict EU data compliance.

[Library Management System provides catalogue and circulation management for public and academic libraries. The Elasticsearch component delivers high-performance full-text search while maintaining EU data residency.]

- Apache Lucene: Provides core indexing and full-text retrieval

- AES-256: Secures data at rest via EU-hosted KMS
- Prometheus: Scrapes metrics for JVM heap and cache ratios

## Rationale
[Separating the search components ensures sub-800ms response times for catalogue searches. Strict encryption, mTLS, and EU-region storage satisfy data residency and security constraints.]

RabbitMQ.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals, adhering strictly to EU-only data residency.

## Key Elements
- Library Patron, Librarian
- Identity Provider (IdP), Payment Gateway, Notification Provider
- Web Frontend (React SPA, Nginx)
- API Gateway (Spring Cloud Gateway)
- Catalogue Service, Circulation Service, Notification Service (Spring Boot, Java 21)
- PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch
- RabbitMQ Components: AMQP Protocol Adapter, Exchanges Component, Queues Component, DLX & Routing Component, Persistent Storage Volume, Alerting and Log Forwarding Component

## Relationships
- Circulation Service -> AMQP Protocol Adapter: Publishes circulation events [AMQP 0-9-1 over mTLS]
- AMQP Protocol Adapter -> Exchanges Component: Routes messages [Internal Erlang messaging]
- Exchanges Component -> Queues Component: Routes messages to persistent queues [Internal Erlang messaging]
- Queues Component -> Notification Service: Delivers notification payloads [AMQP 0-9-1 over mTLS]
- Queues Component -> DLX & Routing Component: Forwards failed/expired messages [Internal Erlang messaging]
- DLX & Routing Component -> Queues Component: Routes to dead-letter queues [Internal Erlang messaging]

## Technology Stack
- Java 21 & Spring Boot: Core microservices framework for robust business logic
- Spring Cloud Gateway: Centralized routing and API management
- Elasticsearch: High-performance indexing ensuring 99th-percentile search response under 800 ms
- PostgreSQL: Relational persistence for transactional catalog and circulation data
- RabbitMQ with Quorum Queues: Asynchronous messaging utilizing Raft consensus across three availability zones for zero data loss
- Erlang/RabbitMQ Core: Message broker engine supporting AMQP 0-9-1 and TLS clustering
- Vault & mTLS: Secure credential management and encrypted service communication

## Rationale
This architecture uses scalable microservices and reactive search tooling to meet strict performance service-level objectives. Furthermore, containerized EU-bound persistent volumes, mutual TLS, and Quorum Queues satisfy compliance and reliability constraints.
